title: Orientation Beacon: persistent, contextual quickstart for Console empty states
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce an "Orientation Beacon" — a small, persistent UI affordance that appears in contextual empty states across the Console (Dashboards, Rollouts, Cost views). The beacon surfaces a 1–3 step quickstart, example templates, and an inline micro-guide (tooltip + short video/gif) tailored to the user's persona and project maturity. Goal: reduce time-to-first-success, lower support tickets for setup, and increase adoption of rollout and cost controls.
background: Current empty states and one-off tutorials are siloed by page. Research and analytics show users drop off at three moments: (1) dashboard creation, (2) rollout policy authoring, (3) interpreting cost breakdowns. Existing guides are long and discoverability is poor. The beacon is inspired by lightweight persistent helpers used in other developer tools but must maintain low visual noise and respect enterprise customers who prefer minimal UI.
design_goals: Decrease setup time for first dashboard by 30%
Surface exactly one actionable next-step in each empty state
Provide templated snippets users can 'inject' into projects
Remain dismissible and remember user preference across sessions
Comply with accessibility contrast and keyboard navigation
proposed_behaviors: Appears only in defined empty states and when user has performed fewer than N interactions
Two visual modes: compact beacon (icon + tooltip) and expanded card (2–3 steps + CTA + sample template),
Personalization signals: account size, role (admin vs. dev), previously completed quickstarts
Telemetry events: shown, expanded, CTA clicked, template used, dismissed
Respect enterprise flag: an admin setting to disable beacons for their org
acceptance_criteria: Beacon appears in Dashboard, Rollouts, and Cost views when corresponding empty state rules match
Expanded card contains at most three steps and a single primary CTA
Beacon adheres to visual system tokens and accessible contrast ratios
Events are emitted for shown/expanded/clicked/dismissed and documented in tracking spec
Design handoff includes Figma frames, copy variants, and component states for compact/expanded/dismissed
comments: 2026-02-12 - Aisha: Initial sketch uploaded to Figma; kept compact iconography to avoid covering key controls.
2026-02-18 - Product (Samir): Suggest we tie beacon triggers to existing 'first N events' metric to avoid false positives.
2026-02-22 - Research (Lina): Prototype user tests (n=8) show users prefer a single example template over multiple choices.
2026-03-01 - Engineering (Priya): Asked for clarified API for template injection and storage of dismissed flag; will parallelize work with frontend component.
2026-03-04 - Accessibility (Marco): Confirmed keyboard focus order and screen reader label patterns; requested larger hit target for compact mode.
review_feedback: PM: Align CTAs with metrics we can track (create dashboard, create rollout, view cost insights).
Eng: Keep expanded card lightweight; avoid heavy images that increase bundle size. Consider lazy-loading gifs.
Design critique: Try a neutral tone for copy to reduce perceived pressure on new users. Two microcopy variants attached.
Legal: Ensure templates do not include any product claims; use neutral example names.
decisions: Limit expanded card to 3 steps and a single primary CTA (Decision 2026-02-20).
Store dismissed state in local storage and server-side (to sync across devices) with opt-out for enterprises (Decision 2026-03-02).
Roll beacon out behind feature flag per environment; default on for new accounts only (Decision 2026-03-03).
tradeoffs: Discoverability vs. clutter: Default to compact beacon to keep UI clean but may reduce feature discovery.
Server-sided tracking increases accuracy but has privacy considerations; mirrored local signal used for immediate UX.
Personalization requires additional user signals which may delay rollout for smaller customers.
